summary.text: Darren Bailey, a southern Illinois farmer and former Republican state representative (2019–2021) and state senator (2021–2023), lost the November 3, 2026 election for governor of Illinois to JB Pritzker.
It was his second run as the Republican nominee for governor, after losing to Pritzker in 2022.

paragraphs.text: Bailey was born in Louisville, Illinois, in 1966, and is a third-generation farmer; he earned an associate degree in agricultural production from Lake Land College.
He and his sons operate Bailey Family Farm, and he and his wife, Cindy, who have been married 39 years, live on the family farm near Louisville.
The couple founded a private Christian school, and he served 17 years on the North Clay Board of Education, 12 of them as president.
They have four children, according to Wikipedia, and his campaign says they have thirteen grandchildren.
Bailey was elected to the Illinois House from the 109th District in 2018 and took office in January 2019.
He won the 55th District seat in the Illinois Senate in 2020 and served there from January 2021, as the Republican spokesperson on the Agriculture Committee.
His campaign says he refused a taxpayer-funded pension as a legislator.
Bailey was the Republican nominee for governor in 2022 and lost to Pritzker.
He won the Republican primary again on March 17, 2026, with Aaron Del Mar of Cook County as his running mate.
During the campaign, his focus was on property taxes, utility costs, public safety and education.
He received 36.6% of the vote to JB Pritzker's 60.1%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
